clue.text: A high-flier in working hours — and he's not alone in that!

definitions.text: A high-flier in working hours — and he's not alone in that!

parts.words: A high-flier in working hours — and he's not alone in that!
parts.note: a person who flies high for a living, yet always shares the cockpit with a colleague

explanation.surface: Praise for an ambitious employee who is not the only star in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a go-getter at work; read literally it is someone who flies aircraft, and the joke is that this flier always has a partner at the controls.
explanation.definitionFit: A second pilot flies alongside the captain, so is never alone on the flight deck.

clue.text: Outspoken article by GBS

parts.note: outspoken means frank, candid
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A frank piece of writing from George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: GBS is George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright; the answer is the title of one of his plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A play written by George Bernard Shaw in 1894, named after its heroine.

clue.text: Drink about ten and there'll be a warning!

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of ten are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A caution that drinking too much port will have consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes ENT, an anagram of TEN, which follows PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or warning of something to come.

clue.text: For the trainee direction is of minimal importance

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A remark that, for a beginner, which way to go hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L plate, so L stands for a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallest in significance; the superlative of little.

clue.text: Keen to get rent fixed, give voice

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of repaired or rearranged, so the letters of rent are reordered

parts.note: to chant is to give voice in song

explanation.surface: A tenant eager to have the rent settled and willing to speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' turns RENT into TREN, followed by CHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen here means sharp or incisive, as a cutting remark is.

clue.text: The beginner puts a point sharp (with little hesitation)

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
tart means sharp in taste
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A novice makes a cutting comment, hesitating only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that begins things, such as a first course or a person who starts a race.

clue.text: A way everyone can ensure a seat at the theatre

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Advice on how every member of the audience can be sure of somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British theatre the stalls are the seats on the ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre seats on the main floor nearest the stage are so named.

clue.text: The fool worker will go around first — or second

indicators.note: the two outer pieces surround the abbreviation for first

parts.note: an ass is a fool
the ant is the crossword's standard worker
1st, written with the numeral as I, gives IST

explanation.surface: A silly employee will take turns at being top or runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will go around' puts IST (1ST with I for 1) inside ASS + ANT. 'First — or second' plays on ranking, but second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a helper or backer, as in a duel or boxing match.

clue.text: Ends achieved by interim arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of interim produces new ones

explanation.surface: Goals reached through a temporary deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' signals the anagram of INTERIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway terminals and other end points; the plural of terminus.

clue.text: Nobel prize winner writing on French rising market

indicators.note: in a down clue the French word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sur is French for on
to market goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A laureate's essay about a French market on the up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SUR into RUS in this down clue. Bertrand Russell won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell, philosopher, won the 1950 Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Tell tales

parts.note: not informing on someone, but relating stories

explanation.surface: An instruction to sneak on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell tales' reads as the idiom for informing on someone; here it means simply to recount stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story or give an account of events.

clue.text: Maintains the estate about right

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters are placed around the second's

parts.note: a person's estate is their assets

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up the family estate properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places ASSETS around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to insist on it or declare it firmly.

clue.text: Indicate new money is wanted just the same

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of indicate are made into a fresh word

parts.note: L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A statement that fresh cash is needed exactly as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns INDICATE into IDENTICA, then L is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly alike, matching in every detail.

clue.text: Shoot and get the bird

explanation.surface: A hunter fires and bags a game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot from a hidden position; also a long-billed wading bird.

clue.text: Moving use of a pen

parts.note: stir is slang for prison, as is pen

explanation.surface: A remark on how emotionally powerful writing with a pen can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is the penitentiary.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and about, in motion or out of bed.

clue.text: Orientals breaking family ties

indicators.note: breaking the word orientals scatters its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: People from the East cutting links with their families.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' signals the anagram of ORIENTALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Kin connected by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Dealing with statistics, get real about reversing impression given

indicators.note: about means the word for real goes around the other piece

parts.note: actual means real

indicators.note: reversing means the word for impression is read backwards

parts.note: an air is an impression or manner given off

explanation.surface: A statistician told to face facts about undoing a false impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns AIR into RIA; 'about' places ACTUAL around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the calculation of insurance risks and premiums using statistical data.

clue.text: Walking around hospital preparing needles for use

indicators.note: around means the walking word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: treading means walking
H is the sign for hospital

explanation.surface: A nurse walks the hospital wards getting needles ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' places TREADING around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing thread through the eyes of needles before sewing.

clue.text: Got a ruler replaced as a means of keeping good order

definitions.text: a means of keeping good order

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of got a ruler are put back in another order

explanation.surface: A new ruler installed to keep things in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' signals the anagram of GOT A RULER.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or official that controls something to keep it working properly.

clue.text: Put right about clothes

parts.note: re means about, concerning
dress means clothes

explanation.surface: Correct what people say about clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy or set right a wrong.

clue.text: Grapple for Greek fruit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Grapple for Greek fruit', uses the answer word as its own definition: GR + APPLE gives the letters but the defining word is missing or misprinted; no source found.

clue.text: Hair in distressingly bad condition

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone's locks in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the run of letters inside 'distressingly'; 'bad condition' adds to the picture of distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock or curl of a person's hair.

clue.text: Look over-clean? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to eye is to look at
wash means clean

explanation.surface: Is that excessively clean? Rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places EYE above WASH in this down answer. 'over-clean' looks like one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug or rubbish talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Hang outlay — back up America initially

indicators.note: initially means the reversed piece comes first
back up means the two-letter abbreviation is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America
to spend is to lay out money

explanation.surface: Hold back spending, an American financial instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back up' turns US into SU, and 'initially' puts it before SPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something from above so it dangles.

clue.text: Plan that will set the medico back

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medico
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A scheme that will cost the doctor dearly.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary version or outline of a document or scheme.

clue.text: Chic to irritate the head

parts.note: to smart is to sting or irritate
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Fashionable style that gives you a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, not the top of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylishness and elegance in dress.

clue.text: Determined to have stone re-cut

indicators.note: re-cut means the letters of stone are cut up and put back differently

explanation.surface: Resolved to have a gemstone reshaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-cut' signals the anagram of STONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something means being resolved to get it.

clue.text: Warble the opening of "Traviata" badly

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ill means badly

explanation.surface: Singing the start of Verdi's opera poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: La Traviata is an opera by Verdi.
explanation.definitionFit: A quavering run of notes in singing or birdsong.

clue.text: Make the most of some achievement

explanation.surface: Advise someone to capitalise on a success.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something fully for profit; also a bold or daring feat.

clue.text: Copy of figures standing in front of London art-gallery

indicators.note: standing in front of means the numerals come before the gallery

parts.note: Roman numerals I, M and I stand for one, a thousand and one
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Reproductions of statues placed outside a London gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like statues but means numerals. The Tate is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce or mimic something.

clue.text: No test's needed anyway — it's topping!

indicators.note: anyway means in any way at all, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive here supplies the letters of tests

explanation.surface: No exam is needed regardless — it's excellent!
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' signals the anagram of NO TESTS. 'topping' means excellent but here describes something worn on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat, worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Party held for a knight

parts.note: a gala is a festive party
had means held, possessed

explanation.surface: A celebration thrown in honour of a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Galahad is the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was a knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.
